title: From options to a written decision with a revisit trigger
captions: This example is made up. A team of three needs a job queue for about 200 jobs a second. They write down three real options.
Before they score anything, they agree what matters: does it handle the load, does the team know it, how much work it is to run, and how easy it is to undo.

These scores are only an example. Each option gets 0 to 3 points per criterion. The table is a tool for talking, not a machine that decides. C wins on load but loses on everything the team must live with.
They choose A, a table in the Postgres database they already run. It is easy to move away from later, so they decide fast.
They write a one-page ADR. It says what they chose, why, and what they give up: A will not grow forever.
The ADR names a clear signal to look again: more than 1,000 jobs a second, or the queue slowing the main database. Then they compare A and B again.
